newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening mostly lower Monday, except for gold which was expected to edge higher on nervousness about a weak U.S. dollar and weak world equity markets.
COMEX December gold was seen opening unchanged to up 20 cents an ounce from Friday's close at $329.50 an ounce, after trading a $329.60-330.90 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $325.90/40 early, compared to the London Monday morning fix at $326.05 and the New York close Friday around $325.80/30 an ounce.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell 23,861 ounces Friday to 922,218 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks were unchanged at 165,395,967 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening down 2.0-3.0 cents an ounce from Friday's close at $4.560, after surging by 15.6 cents Friday.

NYMEX October platinum was expected to open unchanged to $1.00 from Friday's close at $427.50, while NYMEX September palladium was also seen opening unchanged to down $1.00 from the previous close at $205.30.
Overnight TOCOM platinum and palladium prices slipped a little lower, but the physical market remains tight, traders said.
